nodes.label: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking Repository Exploration
nodes.author: Shaoqiu Zhang, Yuhang Wang, Jialiang Liang, Yuling Shi, Wenhao Zeng, Maoquan Wang, Shilin He, Ningyuan Xu, Siyu Ye, Kai Cai, Xiaodong Gu
nodes.rationale: Benchmark isolating repository exploration as line-level evaluation target; given issue and repository, explorer returns ranked list of code regions scored against ground truth derived from successful agent trajectories.

nodes.label: SWE-Explore Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 848 instances across 10 programming languages and 203 repositories; evaluates exploration along coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency dimensions; includes restricted-context validation protocol.

nodes.label: Trajectory-Grounded Supervision
nodes.rationale: Novel annotation method deriving ground truth lines from successful agent trajectories; distills specific code regions solution paths actually consulted with minimal manual annotation.

nodes.label: Ranked Region List Task
nodes.rationale: Formulation of repository exploration as returning ranked list of relevant code regions under fixed line budget; enables comparison of retrievers, search agents, and long-context selectors on common axis.

nodes.label: Restricted-Context Validation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Controlled downstream protocol feeding each explorer's output as only available context to fixed coding agent; verifies that exploration metrics track repair success without requiring explorer to write patches.

nodes.label: SWE-Explore Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for evaluating repository exploration independently from patch generation through ranked, line-level context selection using trajectory-derived supervision.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Annotation via Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Derives supervision from solution-verified agent trajectories rather than manual annotation; keeps only instances with ≥2 successful trajectories from strong LLMs.

nodes.label: SWE-Explore Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: Line-level precision/recall, nDCG@500, HitFile, Context Efficiency, and First Useful Hit; validated against downstream repair behavior.

nodes.label: Explorers Evaluated in SWE-Explore
nodes.rationale: Includes baselines (Oracle, Random), sparse retrievers (BM25, TF-IDF), dense retriever (Potion/RAG), and agentic explorers (Claude Code, Codex, OpenHands, Mini-SWE-Agent, AweAgent, AutoCodeRover, LocAgent, OrcaLoca, CoSIL).

nodes.label: Downstream Validation via Restricted Context
nodes.rationale: Validates exploration metrics by hiding non-selected context and measuring patch-generation resolve rate; shows Context Efficiency has highest Pearson correlation (r=0.950).

nodes.label: Line-Level Evaluation Design
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes file-level hits from line-level recall; most agentic explorers achieve high HitFile but low line-level recall, indicating recall-limited exploration.

nodes.label: CoSIL High-Recall Exploration
nodes.rationale: CoSIL achieves highest non-oracle line-level recall (0.788) and F1 (0.602) via iterative code-graph search; suggests specialized localizers can improve recall.

nodes.label: Context Degradation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Missing core evidence is dominant failure mode; patchers tolerate redundant context once threshold of essential evidence is crossed; threshold-like performance pattern.
